content.en:
The Northern Mountains are divided into the Trans-Himalayas, the Himalayan mountain range, and the Purvanchal (Eastern Hills).

Structural Ranges (N to S)
  • Trans-Himalayas: Karakoram, Ladakh, and Zaskar ranges. Mostly dry, cold desert conditions.
  • Greater Himalayas (Himadri): Highest peaks (Everest, Kanchenjunga). Continuous, composed of granite core.
  • Lesser Himalayas (Himachal): Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mahabharat ranges. Highly rugged, famous hill stations.
  • Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks): Youngest range, made of consolidated sediments, characterized by flat valleys called **Duns** (e.g., Dehradun).
Regional Divisions (W to E)
  • Kashmir/Western Himalayas: Famous for Karewa formations (saffron), cold deserts.
  • Kumaon Himalayas: Between Satluj and Kali rivers; contains peaks like Nanda Devi.
  • Sikkim-Darjeeling Himalayas: Fast-flowing rivers, orchid flora, tea plantations.
  • Arunachal/Eastern Himalayas: High rainfall, deep gorges, home to tribes.
  • Purvanchal: Patkai Bum, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, and Mizo Hills.

title.en: 2. The Northern Plains & The Peninsular Plateau
title.hi: 2. The Northern Plains & The Peninsular Plateau

content.en:
The Plains and the Plateau form the agricultural and mineral backbone of India, respectively.

The Northern Plains (Sub-regions)
  • Bhabar: Porous gravel zone at foothills. Rivers run underground.
  • Terai: Swampy zone where rivers re-emerge; rich in biodiversity.
  • Bhangar: Older clayey alluvium forming upland terraces. Contains calcium nodules called **kankar**.
  • Khadar: Young, fertile alluvial silt renewed annually by floods.
The Peninsular Plateau (Sub-units)
  • Central Highlands: Malwa Plateau, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand. Bordered by Aravalli and Vindhyan ranges.
  • Deccan Plateau: Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana plateaus. Stepped basalt topography.
  • Northeastern Extension: Meghalaya (Garo, Khasi, Jaintia hills) and Mikir hills. Structurally part of Peninsular block.
  • Chotanagpur Plateau: Rich in minerals (coal, iron). Damodar valley coal graben.

title.en: 3. Coastal Plains, Western & Eastern Ghats, and Islands
title.hi: 3. Coastal Plains, Western & Eastern Ghats, and Islands

content.en:
The coastal tracts, mountain borders, and oceanic islands form distinct ecological and structural zones.

Western vs Eastern Ghats
  • Western Ghats (Sahyadris): High, continuous, steep western slope. Thal Ghat, Bhor Ghat, and Pal Ghat are key passes. Highest peak: **Anamudi**.
  • Eastern Ghats: Discontinuous, highly dissected by east-flowing rivers. Average elevation is lower. Highest peak: **Jindhagada / Mahendragiri**.
Coasts and Islands
  • Western Coastal Plains: Narrow, submergent coast. Divided into Konkan, Kannad, and Malabar coasts. Features lagoons (Kayals).
  • Eastern Coastal Plains: Broad, emergent coast. Divided into Northern Circars and Coromandel coast. Famous for large river deltas.
  • Islands: Andaman & Nicobar (tectonic upliftment, volcanic activity like Barren Island) and Lakshadweep (atoll coral islands in the Arabian Sea).

practiceQuestions.q: Which range forms the northernmost limit of the Trans-Himalayan zone in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Karakoram Range is the northernmost range of the Trans-Himalayas, housing peaks like K2.

practiceQuestions.q: The famous peak K2 (Godwin-Austen) is situated in which mountain range?
practiceQuestions.sol: K2, the second highest peak in the world, is located in the Karakoram Range.

practiceQuestions.q: Which major river flows between the Ladakh and Zaskar ranges?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indus River flows through a deep gorge between the Ladakh range to its north and the Zaskar range to its south.

practiceQuestions.q: The highest peak in the Greater Himalayas (Himadri) within India is:
practiceQuestions.sol: Kanchenjunga (8,586m) in Sikkim is the highest peak in the Greater Himalayas located within India.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a structural valley lying between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks?
practiceQuestions.sol: Duns are longitudinal structural valleys formed between the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal) and the Shiwalik range.

practiceQuestions.q: The boundary fault that separates the Shiwalik foothills from the Indo-Gangetic Plain is called the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Himalayan Frontal Thrust (HFT) is the boundary fault separating the Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks) from the Great Plains.

practiceQuestions.q: The swampy, damp, and forest-covered physiographic zone of the Northern Plains is known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Terai is a swampy, marshy belt south of Bhabar where underground streams re-emerge at the surface.

practiceQuestions.q: Which type of alluvium in the Indo-Gangetic Plain contains calcareous concretions called 'kankar'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Bhangar is the older alluvium which lies above flood level and contains calcareous concentrations known as kankar.

practiceQuestions.q: The newer, highly fertile alluvial soil renewed by annual river floods is called:
practiceQuestions.sol: Khadar represents the younger alluvium deposited by rivers on floodplains, which is highly fertile and renewed annually.

practiceQuestions.q: The Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia hills are physiographically part of which division?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya are structurally extensions of the Peninsular Plateau, not the Himalayas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which tectonic gap separates the Meghalaya Plateau from the main Peninsular Plateau block?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Malda Gap (or Garo-Rajmahal Gap) separates the Shillong/Meghalaya Plateau from the Rajmahal Hills of the Peninsular block.

practiceQuestions.q: The highest peak of the Western Ghats (and South India) is:
practiceQuestions.sol: Anamudi (2,695m) in the Anaimalai Hills is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and the entire South India.

practiceQuestions.q: Through which pass does the main railway line connect Mumbai with Nashik?
practiceQuestions.sol: Thal Ghat (Kasara Ghat) connects Mumbai with Nashik, serving as a key corridor through the Western Ghats.

practiceQuestions.q: Which pass separates the Nilgiri Hills to the north from the Anaimalai Hills to the south?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pal Ghat (Palakkad Gap) is a major low pass in the Western Ghats separating the Nilgiris from the Anaimalai hills.

practiceQuestions.q: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and dissected primarily because:
opts: They are older fold mountains that collapsed.
They are cut through by major east-flowing Peninsular rivers.
They were disrupted by Deccan Trap lava flows.
They were eroded by the monsoon winds.
practiceQuestions.sol: Major east-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) have cut wide valleys through the Eastern Ghats, making them highly dissected.

practiceQuestions.q: Which peak is widely cited as the highest point of the Eastern Ghats?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jindhagada Peak (1,690m) in Andhra Pradesh is the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats, though Mahendragiri (1,501m) is also historically famous.

practiceQuestions.q: The coastal plains of Kerala are famous for backwaters and lagoons locally known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: The backwaters of Kerala (Malabar coast) are locally called Kayals, famous for boating and fishing (e.g., Vembanad Lake).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a classic example of an emergent coastal plain in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Eastern Coastal Plain (Coromandel Coast) is a classic example of an emergent coast, characterized by broad deltas.

practiceQuestions.q: The sandy desert area of Rajasthan lying west of the Aravalli range is geologically known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: Marusthali is the extremely arid desert region of Thar in western Rajasthan, characterized by shifting sand dunes.

practiceQuestions.q: The semi-arid transitional plain lying between the desert (Marusthali) and the Aravallis is called:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Rajasthan Bagar (or Bhagar) is the semi-arid steppe/grassland zone east of the core desert, leading to the Aravallis.

practiceQuestions.q: The Lakshadweep islands are situated in which water body?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Lakshadweep archipelago is located in the southeastern Arabian Sea off the coast of Kerala.

practiceQuestions.q: Barren Island, India's only active volcano, is located in which physiographic sub-unit?
practiceQuestions.sol: Barren Island is an active volcano located in the eastern Andaman Sea, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

practiceQuestions.q: Which peak is the highest point of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
practiceQuestions.sol: Saddle Peak (732m) in North Andaman is the highest peak of the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago.

practiceQuestions.q: The southern end of the Nicobar group of islands contains the southernmost point of India, called:
practiceQuestions.sol: Indira Point (formerly Pygmalion Point) on Great Nicobar Island is the southernmost point of Indian territory.

practiceQuestions.q: The Western Ghats act as a major water divide. Rivers like Godavari and Krishna rise on their eastern slopes and flow into the:
practiceQuestions.sol: Because the Peninsular block tilts east, major rivers rising in the Western Ghats flow eastwards across the plateau to enter the Bay of Bengal.

practiceQuestions.q: Which range separates the Narmada Rift Valley from the Tapi Rift Valley?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Satpura Range is a block mountain (horst) that lies between the Narmada rift valley to its north and the Tapi rift valley to its south.

practiceQuestions.q: The plateau characterized by badland topography (ravines) formed by water erosion is the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Malwa Plateau, especially in the Chambal river basin, is famous for its extensive gully erosion creating badland ravines.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the soil type found in the Deccan Trap region?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deccan Trap is covered with fertile black soil (Regur), formed by the weathering of flood basalt lavas.

practiceQuestions.q: The highest peak of the Aravalli Range is:
practiceQuestions.sol: Guru Shikhar (1,722m) near Mount Abu is the highest peak of the ancient Aravalli Range.

practiceQuestions.q: The pass that connects the Kashmir Valley with the Jammu region through the Pir Panjal range is the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Banihal Pass cut through the Pir Panjal range contains the Jawahar Tunnel connecting Jammu with Srinagar.

practiceQuestions.q: Which pass connects Sikkim with Tibet (China) and was reopened for trade in 2006?
practiceQuestions.sol: Nathu La is a famous pass in Sikkim that connects India with Tibet's Chumbi Valley.

practiceQuestions.q: The regional name of the Western Coastal Plain in Maharashtra and Goa is:
practiceQuestions.sol: The northern section of the western coastal plain from Daman to Goa is called the Konkan Coast.

practiceQuestions.q: The southern section of the Western Coastal Plain, stretching from Mangalore to Kanyakumari, is the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The southern stretch of the western coast is the Malabar Coast, characterized by lagoons (Kayals).

practiceQuestions.q: Which delta is NOT located on the Eastern Coastal Plain of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Narmada River flows west and empties into the Arabian Sea through an estuary in Gujarat, not the Eastern Coastal Plain.

practiceQuestions.q: The salt marshy desert area located in the westernmost part of Gujarat is the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Rann of Kutch is a vast seasonal salt marsh located in the Kutch district of Gujarat, divided into Great Rann and Little Rann.

practiceQuestions.q: The Chotanagpur Plateau contains the valley of which river, famous for its coalfields?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Damodar River basin in the Chotanagpur Plateau contains India's premier Gondwana coalfields (e.g., Jharia, Raniganj).

practiceQuestions.q: The regional name of the Eastern Coastal Plain in Odisha is the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The coastal plain in Odisha is known as the Utkal Plain, which includes the Mahanadi delta and Chilika Lake.

practiceQuestions.q: Chilika Lake, India's largest brackish water lagoon, is situated in which state?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chilika Lake is a massive brackish water lagoon situated on the east coast of India in Odisha.

practiceQuestions.q: The Western Ghats are geologically described as:
opts: The faulted western escarpment of the Peninsular plateau block.
Volcanic chains built by submarine hotspots.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Western Ghats are not true mountain ranges but represent the faulted western edge of the Deccan plateau tilting eastward.

practiceQuestions.q: Which range acts as the water divide between the Indus and Ganga river systems?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Delhi Ridge (an extension of the Aravalli range) acts as the primary water divide separating the Indus basin from the Ganga basin.

practiceQuestions.q: The valley of Jhelum River in Kashmir is geologically a basin filled with:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Kashmir Valley is a structural basin filled with thick lacustrine (lake) deposits called Karewas, highly famous for saffron.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following passes connects Himachal Pradesh with Tibet (China)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Shipki La is a mountain pass on the India-China border in Himachal Pradesh, through which the Sutlej River enters India.

practiceQuestions.q: The high peaks of the Lesser Himalayas like Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar lie in which state/UT?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pir Panjal range lies in J&K and Himachal Pradesh, while Dhauladhar is primarily in Himachal Pradesh.

practiceQuestions.q: What type of coral structure characterizes the Lakshadweep Islands?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lakshadweep consists of coral atolls, which are ring-shaped coral reefs enclosing a central lagoon.

practiceQuestions.q: The southernmost island group of India in the Bay of Bengal is:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Nicobar Islands (specifically Great Nicobar) form the southernmost island group of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Which hill range is situated at the tri-junction of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Nilgiri Hills (Blue Mountains) form the meeting point of the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats at the tri-junction of the three states.

practiceQuestions.q: The pass that connects Srinagar with Leh across the Great Himalayan range is:
practiceQuestions.sol: Zoji La is a vital mountain pass that connects Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley with Leh in Ladakh.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following river valleys is NOT a tectonic graben containing Gondwana coal in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Luni Valley in Rajasthan is a desert river system and does not contain Gondwana coal grabens.

practiceQuestions.q: The northern part of the Eastern Coastal Plain, stretching from West Bengal to Andhra Pradesh, is called the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The northern part of the eastern coastal plain is called the Northern Circars, while the southern part is the Coromandel Coast.

practiceQuestions.q: Which peak is the highest in the Nilgiri Hills?
practiceQuestions.sol: Doda Betta (2,637m) is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills, second only to Anamudi in South India.

fact.en: Trap 1: Meghalaya Plateau Connection: The Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau and Karbi Anglong are NOT part of the Himalayas. They are geologically extensions of the **Peninsular Plateau**, separated from it by the Malda Fault (Garo-Rajmahal Gap).
fact.hi: Trap 1: Meghalaya Plateau Connection: The Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau and Karbi Anglong are NOT part of the Himalayas. They are geologically extensions of the **Peninsular Plateau**, separated from it by the Malda Fault (Garo-Rajmahal Gap).

fact.en: Trap 2: Western vs Eastern Ghats Continuity: A common trap is assuming both Ghats are continuous. The **Western Ghats are continuous** and can be crossed only through passes, while the **Eastern Ghats are highly dissected, discontinuous**, and broken by major east-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri).

fact.en: Trap 3: Bhabar vs Terai Characteristics: Bhabar is a dry, porous belt of gravels where streams disappear. Terai is a wet, swampy, marshy forest belt just south of Bhabar where streams re-emerge. Confusing these two is a classic UPSC trap.

fact.en: Trap 4: Island Origins: Lakshadweep islands are of **coral origin** (built up by polyps), whereas the Andaman and Nicobar islands are of **tectonic/volcanic origin** (submarine tertiary mountain ranges rising from the ocean floor).
